title: First meeting and hearing Louis Armstrong
summary: He first met Armstrong in Chicago after Louis had left Oliver, and in New Orleans they knew his records, with 'Cornet Chop Suey' and Bechet's 'Wildcat Blues' heard on every street.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: When was the first time you met Louis Armstrong?
When was the first time you met him?
When you first went to Chicago with King Oliver?
When I went to join King Oliver, but he had left. He used to be with King. And then when he left, the Duke joined Fletcher Henderson. That's when Fletcher came into Chicago, that's when I met Louie.
Is that when you first heard him play?
And what did you think of his playing when you first heard him?

Oh, fantastic. Well, we had records in New Orleans of he and Bechet, and the first thing we heard from Louie was 'Cornet Chop Suey'. That was a biggie in New Orleans. And Sidney's was -- Oh, I can't think of the name of it. (Humming) 'Wildcat Blues'. That was his biggie in New Orleans. You couldn't walk down the street unless you heard one of them. But it was great.
Did you see much of Louie in the years between your first meeting and the time that you joined him much later?
